Rat hole mining in Meghalaya
77. SHRI elAMARAM KAReeM: Will the Minister of MINeS be pleased to 
state:
(a) the time when the centre got information from Meghalaya State Government 
regarding the workers trapped in the rat hole mine;
(b) the steps taken by Central Government immediately after it got the information 
regarding the tragedy;
(c) the reason behind the failure of Government in providing high power pump 
at the earliest to drain out water from the mine;
(d) whether Government has done any effort of find out countries that have 
infrastructure and expertise to save lives trapped in such mines; and

Written Answers to [4 February, 2019]   Unstarred Questions 171
(e) whether Government machinery is a complete failure in stopping rat hole 
mining in Meghalaya?
THe  MINISTe R OF STATe  IN THe  MINISTRy  OF MINe S (SHRI HARIBHAI 
PARTHIBHAI CHAuDHARy): (a) to (d) As per the information provided by Ministry 
of Coal, no information was conveyed by Government of Meghalaya to Ministry 
of Coal (MoC) regarding the accident in the rat hole mine. However, Coal India 
limited (CIl) received a request from the Government of Meghalaya on 26.12.2018 
for assisting in operation to rescue 15 trapped miners in east Jaintia Hills and to 
provide pumps, pipelines and technical persons along with survey personnel. CIl  
intimated MoC on 26.12.2018 (telephonically) and through letter on 27.12.2018 about 
the action being taken by CIl  in this regard.
In consultation with MoC, CIl  has taken immediate action for arranging pumps 
etc. from different subsidiaries of CIl . On 27.12.2018, CIl  dispatched 8 nos. of pumps 
from different subsidiaries of CIl  by road. 4 survey personnel and 6 technical staff 
of CIl  rushed to mishap site of Ksan Coal mine, east Jaintia District of Meghalaya 
by road. Director (Tech), CIl  and General Manager (GM), NeC visited the site.
(e) Ministry of Coal has informed that National Green Tribunal (NGT) has 
banned rat hole mining in the State of Meghalaya and it is for the concerned State 
Government to enforce the said ban. No approval for rat hole mining has been 
granted by the Ministry of Coal anywhere in the country.

an amount of ` 858.99 crore has been released so far to Andhra Pradesh under

Implementation of RGSA
83. DR. SANJA y  SINH: Will the Minister of PANCHA yATI RAJ be pleased 
to state:
(a) the steps taken by Government for effective capacity building of Panchayati 
Raj System in the country;
(b) the details of the steps taken for implementation of Rashtriya Gram Swaraj 
Abhiyan (RGSA) in the country, specifically in Uttar Pradesh; and
(c) the details of the progress of RGSA in the State?
THe  MINIST e R OF STAT e  IN THe  MINISTR y  OF PANCHA y ATI RAJ  
(SHRI PARSHOTTAM RuPAlA): (a) to (c) The Ministry of Panchayati Raj, through 
its erstwhile schemes of Rajiv Gandhi Panchayat Sashaktikaran Abhiyan (RGPSA)/
Capacity Building- Panchayat Sashaktikaran Abhiyan (CB-PSA) had provided assistance 
to the States/uTs for capacity building and training of Panchayat e lected Representatives 
(eRs) and other stakeholders, to enable them to perform their functions, including 
planning and implementation of development programmes, effectively and efficiently. 
The States were also provided support for establishment of Panchayat Resource Centres. 
under these schemes, the States had taken up Capacity Building and Training of 
stakeholders on a large scale including e-enablement, thereby increasing the capacity 
of Panchayati Raj Institutions.
To give further boost to capacity building of eRs and other stakeholders 
of Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs), Government has approved on 21.04.2018 
the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) for 
implementation from 2018-19 to 2021-22 with the primary aim of strengthening 
Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRI's) for achieving Sustainable Development Goals 
(SDGs) with main thrust on convergence with Mission Antyodaya and emphasis on 
strengthening PRI's in the 117 Aspirational Districts.
The Framework for Implementation of RGSA has been prepared and shared with 
the States for implementation of the scheme of RGSA in a meaningful, concerted 
and result oriented manner.
During the current financial year, Annual Action Plans of 32 States/UTs have 
been approved and ` 397.03 crore has been released to 24 States/uTs including  
` 57.15 crore to the State of uttar Pradesh as on 31.1.2019.

Government appointed Legislative Assistants for MPs
85. SHRI SANJA y  SeTH: Will the Minister of PARlIAMeNTAR y  AFFAIRS 
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that many countries provide MPs with qualified 
legislative and Policy Research Assistants for their parliamentary work;
(b) the reason why our Government does not follow such a scheme;
(c) if there is a scheme in place, the details thereof; and
(d) whether there are plans to staff an MPs office adequately with Research 
Assistants, to help him/her discharge his/ her duties in a more informed manner?
THe  MINISTe R OF STAT e  IN THe MINISTR y  OF PARl IAMe NTARy  
AFFAIRS (SHRI VIJA y  GOel): (a) to (d) every country has its own acts and 
rules to determine the salary and facilities to its people representatives according to 
their requirements and conditions. The Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members 
of Parliament Act, 1954 and the Rules made thereunder, which has been enacted 
in pursuance of constitutional provisions, governs salary and allowances of the 
Members of Parliament. The Joint Committee of both Houses, which is constituted 
from time to time, frame rules, after consultation with the Government of India, to 
provide matters for medical facilities, travelling and daily allowances, housing and 
telephone facilities, constituency allowance, office expense allowances, etc. The act 
and the rules made thereunder are amended from time to time in keeping with the 
changing requirements. As per the Members of Parliament (Office Expense Allowance), 
Rules, 1988, lok Sabha Secretariat/Rajya Sabha Secretariat may pay up to rupees 
forty thousand to the person(s) as may be engaged by a Member of Parliament for 
obtaining secretarial assistance for carrying out the parliamentary work and one such 
person shall be computer literate duly certified by the Member.

87. SHRI V . VIJA yASAI ReDDy : Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT 
AND HIGHWAyS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Ministry has finally approved Anantapur-Amaravati 
expressway recently;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the Ministry has agreed to share fifty per cent 
cost of land acquisition and present status of land acquisition;
(c) the procedure being followed in similar projects in other parts of the country 
with regard to land acquisition and sharing of costs;
(d) details of plan of action to complete the above expressway; and
(e) reasons for narrowing the expressway from 200 meters to 100 meters?
THe MINISTeR OF STATe IN THe MINISTR y  OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND 
HIGHWAyS (SHRI MANSuKH MANDA VIy A): (a) to (e) The Ministry of Road 
Transport and Highways has held 2 meetings with officers of Government of Andhra 
Pradesh on 13-08-2018 and 23-10-2018 regarding the development of an Access 
Controlled Green Field expressway connecting the new capital city of Amaravati to 
Anantapuramu in the State of Andhra Pradesh. The alignment of the aforesaid road 
stretch has been finalized with a length of approximately 384 kms. and 100m Right 
of Way to develop the expressway initially as 4-lane expressway with a provision 
of upgradation/expansion to 8-lane in future depending upon the traffic requirement. 
Government of Andhra Pradesh has agreed to transfer the government land free of 
cost and bear 50% of the cost of the land to be acquired. Further, the Government 
of Andhra Pradesh has also agreed to obtain requisite statutory clearances (i.e.  
environmental, forest, wildlife etc.) so that the approval/award of civil work/execution 
of work for the aforesaid expressway is taken up expeditiously. land acquisition 
proceedings for the expressway have been initiated. Similar projects in other parts 
of the country (including Amaravati-Anantapuramu expressway) are taken up subject 
to the State Government has acquired 50% land by the time the DPR is ready and 
where 90% land has been acquired at the time of award of the project.

(c) and (d)  As per the study conducted by International Road Assessment

IRAP studied 1397.4 km. of Delhi-Mumbai corridor (divided road) and 1318.3 
km. of Mumbai-Chennai corridor (divided road). The IRAP study provides star rating 
of the road sections considering more than 50 parameters of the road cross-section 
and geometry. It was found out that 30% of the length was having less than 3-Star 
rating (where 5-Star means safest and 1-Star means unsafe). Similarly, for Mumbai-
Chennai corridor 50% of the length was found to be of less than 3-Star rating.

The National Highway passing through urban/semi-urban areas or developed 
villages required pedestrian and NMT facilities, which are absent as per study. Also, 
traffic is moving through the intersections at speed higher than 60 kmph. According 
to i-RAP, for the design speed of 100 kmph. for the two corridors, and based on 
operating speed of 85th percentile speed, the roads were considered to be unsafe 
for motor vehicles for 30% and 50% length respectively.
(e) The Government has made necessary amendment in Section 135 and Schedule 
VII of Companies Act as well as the provisions of the Companies (Corporate Social 
Responsibility Policy) Rule 2014 which inter alia envisage that every qualifying 
company requires spending of at least 2% of its average net profit for the immediately 
preceding 3 financial years on CSR activities. These activities also include road safety. 
The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has taken a number of steps to 
prevent road accidents and road accident fatalities as per details mentioned under:–
(i) Government has launched a mobile app for highway users i.e. “Sukhady atra 
1033” which enables highways users to report potholes and other safety 
hazards on National Highways including accidents.
(ii) Rectification of identified Black spots.
(iii) Road Safety Audits are being carried out at all stages of development 
of the highway i.e. design/construction/operation stages.
(iv) Facilities such as Foot Over bridges and under passes are being provided 
wherever required, for safe crossing of pedestrians and other road users.
(v) Road Safety Week is observed every calendar year for spreading awareness 
about safer behaviour of road users on National Highways.
(vi) The Government has approved a National Road Safety Policy. This Policy 
outlines various policy measures such as promoting awareness, establishing 
road safety information data base, encouraging safer road infrastructure 
including application of intelligent transport, enforcement of safety laws.
(vii) The Ministry has constituted Group of Ministers of State Transport 
Ministers to examine the best practices of Transport and suggest issues to 
improve road safety. Based on the recommendation of Group of Minister, 
the Ministry introduced Motor Vehicle (Amendment) Bill, 2017 covering 
entire gamut of road safety. 
(viii) The Ministry has formulated a multi-pronged strategy to address the issue 
of road safety based on 4 ‘e’s viz. education, engineering (both of roads 
and vehicles), enforcement and emergency Care.

stage. 
(x) The threshold for four laning of national highway has been reduced from

of stretches of State Highways has been identified for conversion to 
national highways.
(xi) Setting up of model driving training institutes in States and refresher 
training to drivers of Heavy Motor Vehicle in the unorganized sector.
(xii) Advocacy/Publicity campaign on road safety through the electronic and 
print media.
(xiii) Tightening of safety standards for vehicles like Seat Belts, anti-lock 
braking system etc.
(xiv) High priority has been accorded to identification and rectification of black 
spots (accident prone spots) on national highways.
(xv) As a measure of supplementing the efforts of States/ uTs for minimizing the 
accident potential at the identified locations/stretches through engineering 
improvement on State roads, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
had taken a decision to sanction road safety works on State roads with 
an earmarked allocation of 10% of funds allocated to the State roads 
under Central Road Fund. 
(xvi) Ministry has delegated powers to Regional Officers of MORTH for 
technical approval to the detailed estimates for rectification of identified

ensure safety of road users.
(xvii) Ministry had issued guidelines  vide O.M. dated 14.1.2016 for taking up

(xix) A Certification Course for Road Safety Auditors has been commenced 
in Indian Academy of Highway engineers (IAHe) and 42 Auditors are 
certified. 
(xx) Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has constituted a District Road 
Safety Committee in each district of the country to promote awareness 
amongst road users under the chairmanship of Hon’ble Member of 
Parliament (lok Sabha) from the district.

99. DR. SANJA y  SINH: Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND 
HIGHWAyS be pleased to state: 
(a) details of the steps taken for ensuring the safe driving on National Highways; 
(b) whether Government has any plan for implementation of 'lane driving' 
mandatory throughout the country; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
THe  MINIST e R OF STAT e  IN THe  MINISTR y  OF ROAD TRANSPORT 
AND HIGHWAyS (SHRI MANSuKH MANDA VIy A): (a) to (d) The Ministry of 
Road Transport and Highway has introduced Motor Vehicle (Amendment) Bill in the 
House. The bill contains several provisions to strengthen road safety by addressing 
all relevant areas such as vehicles, roads, trauma care and road discipline.
Apart from above manual, all states have been mandated to form their own road 
safety policy for traffic and transport management based on their own geographical 
and special conditions. All Hilly States have formed Road safety policy. 
The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways administers different schemes to 
improve road safety scenario in the country. These schemes are setting up of Institute 
of Driving and Training Research (IDTR), setting up Inspection and Certification 
(I and C) Centre, Publicity and Awareness campaign, National Highways Accident 
Relief Service Scheme, Road Safety and Pollution Testing equipment and Programme 
Implementation. 
The Government has constituted the National Road Safety Council as the apex 
body to take policy decisions in matters of road safety. Road safety is a multi-sectoral 
and multi- dimensional issue requiring a multipronged approach at various levels. 
The Ministry has introduced Motor Vehicle (Amendment) Bill in the lok Sabha 
covering entire gamut of road safety including drunken driving. The Bill inter alia 
envisages to enhance the penalty amount for drunk and driving under section 185 

Written Answers to [4 February, 2019]   Unstarred Questions 229
of the Motor Vehicle Act. Besides, the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
administer Motor Vehicles (MV) Act 1988 and Central Motor Vehicle Rules (CMVR) 
1989. However, its provisions are enforced by the States/uTs.
The Ministry has taken a number of steps to prevent such road accidents as 
per details mentioned under:–
(i) The Government has launched a mobile app for highway users i.e.  
“Sukhad yatra 1033” which enables highways users to report potholes 
and other safety hazards on National Highways including accidents.
(ii) Rectification of identified Black spots.
(iii) Road Safety Audits are being carried out at all stages of development 
of the highway i.e. design/construction/operation stages.
(iv) Facilities such as Foot Over bridges and underpasses are being provided 
wherever required, for safe crossing of pedestrians and other road users.
(v) Road Safety Week is observed every calendar year for spreading awareness 
about safer behavior of road users on National Highways.
(vi) The Government has approved a National Road Safety Policy. This 
Policy outlines various policy measures such as promoting awareness, 
establishing road safety information data base, encouraging safer road 
infrastructure including application of intelligent transport, enforcement 
of safety laws.
(vii) The Ministry has constituted Group of Ministers of State Transport 
Ministers to examine the best practices of Transport and suggest issues 
to improve road safety. Based on the recommendation of Group of 
Ministers, the Ministry introduced Motor Vehicle (Amendment) Bill 2017 
covering entire gamut of road safety. 
(viii) The Ministry has formulated a multi-pronged strategy to address the 
issue of road safety based on 4 ‘e’s viz. education, engineering (both 
of roads and vehicles), enforcement and emergency Care.
(ix) Road safety has been made an integral part of road design at planning 
stage. 
(x) The threshold for four laning of national highway has been reduced 
from 15,000 Passenger Car units (PCus) to 10,000 PCus. About 52,000 
km. of stretches of State Highways has been identified for conversion 
to national highways.
(xi) Setting up of model driving training institutes in States and refresher 
training to drivers of Heavy Motor Vehicle in the unorganized sector.

(xii) Advocacy/Publicity campaign on road safety through the electronic and 
print media.
(xiii) Tightening of safety standards for vehicles like Seat Belts, anti-lock 
braking system etc.
(xiv) High priority has been accorded to identification and rectification of 
black spots (accident prone spots) on national highways.
(xv) As a measure of supplementing the efforts of States/uTs for minimizing 
the accident potential at the identified locations/stretches through 
engineering improvement on State roads, Ministry of Road Transport 
and Highways had taken a decision to sanction road safety works on 
State roads with an earmarked allocation of 10% of funds allocated to 
the State roads under Central Road Fund.
(xvi) Ministry has delegated powers to Regional Officers of MORTH for 
technical approval to the detailed estimates for rectification of identified 
Road Accident black spots for expediting the rectification process to 
ensure safety of road users.
(xvii) Ministry had issued guidelines  vide O.M. dated 14.1.2016 for taking up 
of Road Safety Audits on National Highways either as part of ePC/
BOT projects or as stand-alone Road Safety Audits.
(xviii) Guidelines for pedestrian facilities on National Highways for persons 
with disabilities have also been issued to all States/uTs. 
(xix) A Certification Course for Road Safety Auditors has been commenced 
in Indian Academy of Highway engineers (IAHe) and 42 Auditors are 
certified. 
(xx) Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has constituted a District Road 
Safety Committee in each district of the country to promote awareness 
amongst road users under the chairmanship of Hon’ble Member of 
Parliament (lok Sabha) from the district.

Concerns over implementation of MGNREGA
104. SHRI G. C. CHANDRASHeKHAR: Will the Minister of RuRAl  
DeVelOPMeNT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Mahatma Gandhi National Rural employment Guarantee Act 
(MGNREGA) scheme is facing a severe fund crunch and the scheme faces difficulties 
in meeting the demand for work and paying wages on time;
(b) if so, details thereof;
(c) whether 250 lawmakers and activists have written to the Prime Minister 
raising concerns over implementation of the MGNReGA scheme;
(d) if so, the details thereof and action taken thereon;
(e) whether there is an urgent need for strengthening MGNReGA, amid a 
situation of distress across rural India with massive unemployment; and
(f) if so, steps being taken by Government to improve lives of rural workers?

Written Answers to [4 February, 2019]   Unstarred Questions 253
THe MINISTeR OF STATe IN THe MINISTR y  OF RuRAl  DeVelOPMeNT 
(SHRI RAM KRIPAl  yADA V): (a) and (b) The Ministry releases funds to the State/
uT based on the basis of the agreed to labour Budget, opening balance, pending 
liabilities of the previous year for the financial year, if any, and overall performance. 
Fund release to States/ uTs is a continuous process and Central Government is 
committed in making funds available keeping in view the demand for work. During 
F.y. 2018-19 (as on 31.01.2019), ` 54050.64 crore has been released under the 
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNReGS) to 
States/uTs. The Ministry seeks additional amount for MGNReGA as and when 
required for meeting the demand for work on the ground.
(c) and (d) Ministry of Rural Development has been received various representation/ 
references regarding implementation of the MGNREGS from Prime Minister’s Office. 
Since the responsibility of implementation of MGNReGA is vested with the State 
Governments, all representation/ references are forwarded to the concerned State 
Governments for taking appropriate action including investigation, as per law.
(e) and (f) The Government has taken steps to strengthen implementation of 
MGNReGA from time to time. These include:–
(i) Implementation of National electronic Fund Management System (Ne-
FMS) and focus on Aadhaar Based Payment system, streamlining fund 
flow mechanism, and monitoring of timely payment of wages to workers.
(ii) Training of Barefoot Technicians, capacity building of MGNReGA 
functionaries such as State Technical Resource Team/District Technical 
Resource Team/Block Technical Resource Team on Mission Water 
Conservation works, training on Geo-MGNReGA, training to Finance 
officers of States on preparation of fund proposals etc.
(iii) Framework for strengthening of monitoring mechanism developed and 
advisories issued for inspection of MGNReGA works by State, District 
and Block level officials and National Level Monitors.
(iv) The Ministry has initiated Job Cards (JCs) verification of MGNREGA 
workers to weed out the bogus and duplicates JCs.
(v) Auditing Standards have been issued and States have been advised 
to establish independent Social Audit units, conduct Social Audit as 
per Audit of Scheme Rules, training of Village Resource Persons for 
conducting Social Audit etc.
(vi) A path breaking initiative for improved planning, effective monitoring 
and greater transparency with the use space technology for geo-tagging 
of MGNReGA assets has also been launched.

Use of technology for construction of roads in rural areas
114. SHRI NARA yAN lA l  PANCHARIy A: Will the Minister of Ru RAl  
DeVelOPMeNT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has taken any measures to rope in technology for 
monitoring of construction of roads in rural areas;

270 Written Answers to [RAJyA SABHA] Unstarred Questions
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether Government has proposed to use satellite imagery to bring in 
transparency, accountability and efficiency in construction of roads in rural areas; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?
THe MINISTeR OF STATe IN THe MINISTR y  OF RuRAl  DeVelOPMeNT 
(SHRI RAM KRIPAl  yADA V): (a) to (d) Various measures have been taken by the 
Ministry of Rural Development to use technology for monitoring the construction of 
roads in rural areas. An On-line Management, Monitoring and Accounting System 
(OMMAS) (www.omms.nic.in) has also been developed, which is being used as an 
effective management tool for customized management and performance reports at 
State and National level.
Ministry has also initiated a project for validation of completed and ongoing 
roads through the combined use of geo-informatics, Satellite imageries and Mobile 
technology. Further, the Ministry has launched “Meri Sadak” Mobile App for Citizen 
Feed Back System for PMGSy  roads on 20th July, 2015 for citizens to enable them 
to submit their feedback related to slow pace, abandoned works, poor quality of 
works of PMGSy  roads by way of capturing roads/bridges photographs. The Nodal 
Officers are required to provide an interim reply to the citizen within 7 days from 
the receipt of the feedbacks. A final Action Taken Report is required to be submitted 
to the citizen within a period of 60 days.
The Ministry undertook a proof of concept exercise in 10 districts for using 
satellite imageries for validating the roads sanctioned under PMGS y. Based on 
the same, the concept was up-scaled by the Ministry with signing of a Tripartite 
Agreement on 07.03.2017 with National Remote Sensing Centre under Indian Space 
Research Organization, Hyderabad and Centre for Geo- Informatics Application in 
Rural Development of National Institute of Rural Development and Panchayat Raj, 
Hyderabad to use geo-informatics and satellite imagery, to verify the progress of 
implementation as reported electronically by the States.
The project started in January, 2018. The project will see the use of Geo 
Informatics System, Satellite imageries and Mobile technology for the validation of 
the completed and ongoing roads in terms of status of the sanctioned project and 
achievement of connectivity as reported by the states. In order to facilitate ground 
truthing, a mobile application called geo-pmgsy has been developed by the Ministry 
which will be used in the project for ground truthing.

115. DR. VIKAS MAHATMe: Will the Minister of RuRAl  DeVelOPMeNT 
be pleased to state:
(a) the amount of funds raised through various sources for the Saansad Adarsh 
Gram yojana and details thereof;
(b) whether a Committee has been constituted for the purpose of creating 
operational guidelines for the scheme and if so, details thereof; and
(c) whether Government has faced any challenges in implementing the scheme, 
and if so, the plans to address them?
THe MINISTeR OF STATe IN THe MINISTR y  OF RuRAl  DeVelOPMeNT 
(SHRI RAM KRIPAl  y ADA V): (a) under the Saansad Adarsh Gram y ojana 
framework, the development of Gram Panchayats is envisaged through convergence 
and implementation of existing Government Schemes and Programmes under the 
administrative control of respective Ministries without allocating additional funds. 
The amount of funds raised through various sources for the Saansad Adarsh Gram 
yojana Gram Panchayats is not maintained centrally.
(b) The Scheme Guidelines have been prepared in 14 languages (english, Hindi, 
Gujarati, Kannada, Marathi, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, urdu, Malayalam, Assamese, 
Kashmiri, Konkani and Oriya) and distributed to all stakeholders in October 2014. 
The roles and responsibilities of different functionaries of SAGy  have been described 
under the Chapter 10 of Guidelines.
(c) The Gram Panchayats adopted under SAGy  prepare Village Development 
Plans (VDP) through a participatory process under the guidance of Hon’ble Members 
of Parliament. The VDP includes prioritised time-bound activities to achieve holistic 
progress of the village. Out of the 1,466 Gram Panchayats identified under SAGY , 
1,206 Gram Panchayats have uploaded their VDPs containing 65,252 projects, as 
per data available on SAGy  website (http://saanjhi.gov.in) on 30 January 2019 and 
implementation of 33,428 (51%) projects has been completed. The following initiatives 
have been inter alia taken for better implementation of the Scheme:–
 ● The guidelines of as many as 26 Central Schemes have been amended or 
enabled to accord priority for the SAGy  Gram Panchayats. A compilation 
of 223 Central Sector/Centrally Sponsored and 1,806 State Schemes for 
convergence under SAGY for the benefit of Members of Parliament, District 
and Village level officials have been prepared.

 ● Ministry has published a document named ‘SAHyOG’ as an indicative 
guidance document with the essential information on the existing social 
security schemes collated from respective Ministries to enrich the knowledge 
of villagers and village level functionaries to achieve 100% enrollment into 
the social/financial Security Schemes in SAGY Gram Panchayats.
 ● The Ministry of Rural Development has coordinated with other Central 
Ministries/Departments for ensuring provision of four key basic services viz. 
power, drinking water, roads and education in all SAGy  Gram Panchayats.
 ● The Ministry organised capacity building exercises for more than 1200 SAGy  
functionaries recognising that the implementation of SAGy  requires highly 
motivated and knowledgeable personnel.
 ● Further, Ministry has met with the representatives of Industry and Professional 
Associations linked with Ministry of Corporate Affairs and oriented them on 
the opportunities presented by SAGy , Mission Antyodaya and other schemes 
for converging private/corporate investments with the government initiatives

Return of Indian scientists to work in India
120. SHRI NARA yAN lAl  PANCHARIy A: Will the Minister of SCIeNCe 
AND TeCHNOlOGy  be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has any information regarding Indian scientists returning 
to India;
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether there has been any increase/decrease in the number of Indian 
scientists who are returning to work in India;
(d) if so, details thereof;
(e) whether Government has taken any measures to stop migration of Indian 
scientists to other countries; and

302 Written Answers to [RAJyA SABHA] Unstarred Questions
(f) if so, details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?
THe MINISTeR OF SCIeNCe AND TeCHNOlOGy  (DR. HARSH V ARDHAN): 
(a) to (d) Government is aware of the fact that many Indian scientists are returning 
to India through different schemes/programmes of the Government. The Indian 
origin scientists return to India has increased to 649 in number in the year 2012 to 
17 as compared to 243 in the period 2007-12. The increase of number of Indian 
scientists returning to India is primarily due to proactive schemes and programmes 
instituted by the Government. Department of Science and Technology (DST) through 
Ramanujan Fellowship Scheme and the Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired 
Research (INSPIRe) Faculty Scheme and Department of Biotechnology (DBT) through 
Ramalingaswami re-entry Fellowship provide attractive avenues and opportunities to 
Indian researchers of high calibre, who are residing in foreign countries, to work in 
Indian Institutes/universities of their respective interest and domain. In addition to 
assured fellowship and research grant for a period of five years for the scientists, 
provisions to seek other competitive research grants from the Government made these 
schemes more attractive and popular.
(e) and (f) Schemes/Programmes such as Fund for improvement of S&T 
infrastructures in universities and higher educational institutions (FIST) to build research 
infrastructure for enhancing research capabilities, Core Research Grant, Research 
fellowships such as JC Bose and Swarnajayanti are targeted at scientific community 
to continue global level research in the country. Special attention has been given to 
young scientists for making them independent and motivate them to remain in the 
country through schemes like early Career Research Award, National Postdoctoral 
Fellowship etc. The propitious policy frameworks developed by the Government and 
the sophisticated research facilities available in our academic and research institutions 
stop migration of Indian scientists to other countries.

130. SHRI D. KuPeNDRA ReDDy : Will the Minister of WATeR ReSOuRCeS,

(a) whether it is a fact that availability of water in many regions of the country 

Written Answers to [4 February, 2019]   Unstarred Questions 313
is way below the national average and are considered as water stressed/water scarce 
region;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor; 
(c) whether the Central Government has identified such water stressed/water 
scarce regions of the country; 
(d) if so, the names of those regions, State-wise; and 
(e) the effective steps taken/being taken by the Central Government to mitigate 
the water scarcity and drought conditions of these regions?
THe MINISTeR OF STATe IN THe MINISTR y  OF WATeR ReSOuRCeS, 
RIVe R De Vel OPMe NT AND GANGA Re JuVe NATION (SHRI ARJuN RAM 
MeGHWAl): (a) to (e) The average annual water potential in the country has been 
assessed as 1869 Billion Cubic Meters (BCM). Due to topographical and other factors, 
the utilizable water availability is limited to 1137 BCM per annum, comprising of 
690 BCM of surface water and 447 BCM of replenishable ground water. 
The average annual water availability of any region or country is largely 
dependent upon hydro-meteorological and geological factors and is generally constant. 
However, water availability per person is dependent on population of the country 
and for India, per capita water availability in the country is reducing progressively 
due to increase in population. The average annual per capita water availability in 
the years 2001 and 2011 was assessed as 1816 cubic meters and 1545 cubic meters 
respectively which may reduce further to 1340 and 1140 in the years 2025 and 2050 
respectively. Annual per-capita water availability of less than 1700 cubic meters is 
considered as water stressed condition, whereas annual per-capita water availability 
below 1000 cubic meters is considered as a water scarcity condition. Due to high 
temporal and spatial variation of precipitation, the water availability of many regions 
of the country is much below the national average and may result in water stress/
scarce conditions. 
The specific identification of water stressed/water scarce regions has not been 
undertaken. However, as per the assessment of ground water resources carried out 
in the year 2013, out of the total 6584 numbers of assessment units (Block/Taluks/ 
Mandals) in the country, 1034 units have been categorized as ‘Over-exploited’, where 
ground water extraction is more than net ground water availability and there is 
significant long-term decline in water levels. State-wise number of ‘Over-exploited’ 
units are given in the Statement (See below).

314 Written Answers to [RAJyA SABHA] Unstarred Questions
Water being a State subject, steps for augmentation, conservation and efficient 
management of water resources including mitigation of water scarcity are primarily 
undertaken by the respective State Governments. In order to supplement the efforts of 
the State Governments, Central Government provides technical and financial assistance 
to them through various schemes and programmes. Central Government has taken 
various steps to mitigate water scarcity and drought conditions in the country.
Central Government has formulated a National Perspective Plan (NPP) for Water 
Resources Development which envisages transfer of water from water surplus basins 
to water deficit basins to improve availability of water. 
Central Government has launched Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee y ojana 
(PMKSy) in 2015-16 which aims to enhance physical access of water on farm and 
expand cultivable area under assured irrigation, improve farm water use efficiency, 
introduce sustainable water conservation practices, etc. During 2016-17, 99 on-going 
Major/Medium irrigation projects under PMKSY-Accelerated Irrigation Benefits 
Programme (AIBP) having ultimate irrigation potential of 76.03 lakh hectares 
have been prioritized in consultation with States, for completion in phases up to  
December, 2019.
Central Government has formulated National Water Policy (NWP), 2012 which 
inter alia recommends conservation, promotion and protection of water and highlights 
the need for augmenting the availability of water through rain water harvesting, direct 
use of rainfall and other management measures. The NWP, 2012 has been sent to all 
States/union Territories and the concerned Central Ministries for appropriate action.
Central Government has launched the National Water Mission with the objective of 
conservation of water, minimizing wastage and ensuring its more equitable distribution 
both across and within States through integrated water resources development and 
management. 
Some initiatives/measures taken by the Central Government for conservation and 
improvement of availability of water are available at the URL:http://mowr.gov.in/sites/
default/files/MeasuresForGW-Depletion_1.pdf

(a) and (b) Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) had carried out Biological Water 
Quality Monitoring (BWQM) at 41 locations along main stem of river Ganga from 
Haridwar Barrage, uttarakhand to Garden Reach, West Bengal during Pre-monsoon 
(April-June, 2017) and 39 locations during Post-monsoon (December 2017-March, 
2018). A draft report based on preliminary bio-monitoring study was prepared on the 
basis of biological parameters using benthic macro-invertebrates as indicator organisms 
following Biological Water Quality Criteria (BWQC). 
The first round of monitoring was conducted in 2014-15 to formulate Standard 
Operating Procedures (SOPs) as well as understand the baseline status. Depending on 
the findings of 2014-15, similar exercise was carried out during 2015-16 to validate 
the findings and classify the river water quality status using the Biological Water 
Quality Criteria developed by CPCB based on combination of internationally accepted

parameters viz. Saprobic Score and Diversity Score. However, BWQC has not been 
notified by the Government. BWQC is qualitative criteria rather than quantitative and 
making any inference on qualitative assessment requires detailed collaboration with 
physico-chemical quality findings also which is quantitative parametric monitoring.
As per the assessment in the draft report, biological water quality at Haridwar 
barrage (uK-6) was found to be Clean (BWQC Class A) in Post-monsoon of 2017-18. 
The biological water quality of main stream of River Ganga remains stable in the 
entire stretch (Moderate Pollution category; BWQC Class C) except for 3 locations 
downstream of Jagjeetpur STP; downstream of Kannauj after confluence with River 
Ramganga and River east Kali and Pandu river where biological water quality was

(b) if so, the reasons therefor;

(d) the plan of Government for cleaning and rejuvenation of the other important 
rivers?
THe MINISTeR OF STATe IN THe MINISTR y  OF WATeR ReSOuRCeS, 
RIVeR DeVelOPMeNT AND GANGA ReJuVeNATION (DR. SATy A PAl  
SINGH): (a) and (b) No, Sir. Though the cleaning of river is a continuous process, 
the actions taken by the Government under Namami Gange Programme is resulting 
in improvement of the river water quality. under Namami Gange Programme, the 
Government of India is supplementing the efforts of the State Governments in cleaning 
the rivers by providing financial assistance. The Central Government approved the 
''Namami Gange Program'' on 13th May, 2015 with an outlay of ` 20,000 crore as 
a comprehensive approach to rejuvenate the river Ganga and its tributaries, under one 
umbrella, by consolidating the existing ongoing efforts and planning for a concrete 
action plan for the future.
(c) and (d) The Namami Gange Programme covers short term, medium term and 
long term activities. under short term activities certain entry level activities which 
cover development of ghats crematoria and river surface cleaning activities etc have 
been taken up. under medium term activities, existing Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs) 
and Effluent Treatment Plants (ETPs) are being upgraded and new STP and ETPs are 
being established. Beside, rural sanitation has been taken up in the villages on the 
banks of river Ganga. The long term action plan involves restoration of wholesomeness 
of river Ganga and maintaining the ecological ad geological integrity of river. The 
projects under short term activities are on track and are to be completed by March 
2019. under medium and long term activities, variety of coordinated activities meant 
for cleaning of river Ganga including treatment of municipal sewage, treatment of 
industrial effluent, drain bio-remediation, river surface cleaning, rural sanitation, 
river front development, afforestation and biodiversity conservation, public outreach 
etc. have been taken up. So far, a total of 261 projects have been sanctioned at an 
estimated cost of ` 25,563 crore for various activities. Out of these, 76 projects 
have been completed.
Ministry of environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoeF and CC) has been 
supplementing the efforts of the State Governments in abatement of pollution in 
identified stretches of various rivers under the centrally sponsored scheme of National 
River Conservation Plan (NRCP) on cost sharing basis between the Central and State 
Governments. Various pollution abatement schemes taken up under NRCP, inter alia, 
include interception and diversion of raw sewage, construction of sewerage systems, 

328 Written Answers to [RAJyA SABHA] Unstarred Questions
setting up of sewage treatment plants, low cost sanitation, river front/bathing ghat 
development, etc. Implementation of NRCP works has led to reduction in pollution 
load draining into rivers as well as improving the environmental and sanitation 
conditions in the towns in which the programmes have been implemented. 
NRCP has so far covered polluted stretches of 33 rivers in 76 towns spread over 
15 States in the country at a sanctioned cost of ` 4801.57 crore and Central share 
of ` 2337.73 crore has been released to the State Governments for implementation 
of various pollution abatement schemes. Sewage treatment capacity of 2520.43 Mld 
(Million litres per Day) has been created so far under the NRCP.
The strategies for conservation and rejuvenation of rivers in the country are 
revised from time to time in consultation with the State Governments and are ongoing 
processes. Works are taken up in identified polluted river stretches under the National 
River Conservation Plan on the basis of conformity with the guidelines, pollution 
status, prioritization, willingness of the State Governments to contribute their matching 
share and availability of Plan funds and incorporation of appropriate strategies.

is providing full assistance to the identified athletes for intensive coaching through 
national coaching camps organised by the Sports Authority of India (SAI) besides 
providing foreign exposures/competitions under the Scheme of Assistance to National 
Sports Federations (NSFs).
Further, the Ministry of youth Affairs and Sports is implementing Target Olympic 
Podium Scheme (TOPS) within overall ambit of National Sports Development Fund 
(NSDF) for providing financial assistance to elite athletes included in TOPS for their 
customized training in world class training institutes/academies within the country 
and abroad.
TOPS gives focused attention to identify, groom and prepare potential medal 
prospects for Olympics/Paralympics 2020. The training programme and other 
requirements of the athletes, selected under TOPS, are considered by the designated 
Committee in Mission Olympic Cell (MOC), headed by Director General, Sports 
Authority of India (SAI).
(c) No such complaint regarding food and accommodation during participation 
in sports events abroad has been received in recent past from athletes.
(d) SAI has signed agreements with foreign coaches. Foreign Coaches, engaged 
with SAI, are also to train two (2) Indian coaches to upgrade their knowledge/ 
technical skill etc. At present, 18 foreign coaches and 6 foreign support staff have 
been engaged with SAI.
Target Olympics Podium Scheme
147. KuMARI SelJA: Will the Minister of yOuTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS 
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has made any proposal for increase in the budgetary 
allocation to the Ministry of youth Affairs and Sports;
(b) the funds allocated, received and spent under Target Olympic Podium (TOP) 
Scheme, till date;
(c) the list of sportspersons who have been provided assistance under the Scheme, 
till date;
(d) the criteria in place for choosing sportspersons who will be provided assistance 
under TOPS for Tokyo Olympics 2020;
(e) whether Ministry has finalised a list of the sportspersons for Tokyo Olympics 
2020 who will be provided assistance; and

Written Answers to [4 February, 2019]   Unstarred Questions 343
(f) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?
THe MINISTeR OF STATe OF THe MINISTR y  OF yOuTH AFFAIRS AND 
SPORTS (COL. RAJYA V ARDHAN SINGH RATHORE): (a) For the current financial 
year 2018-19, there is no proposal to increase the budgetary allocation to the Ministry 
of youth Affairs and Sports.
(b) and (c) Target Olympic Podium (TOP) Scheme is implemented within 
overall ambit of National Sports Development Fund (NSDF). Funds to the extent 
of ` 35 crore has been released to SAI since 2014-15 and as on 31st January, 
2019 for funding the training of athletes included under TOP Scheme. In addition, 
payments to the tune of ` 11.85 crore have been made towards payment of out of 
pocket allowance (OPA) to the sportspersons included in TOP scheme at the rate of  
` 50,000 per month. The details of sportspersons who have been provided assistance 
under the TOP Scheme till date is given in the Statement (See below).
(d) to (f) For inclusion of sportspersons in Target Olympic Podium Scheme 
(TOPS), detailed analysis of probable Indian sportspersons identified for Tokyo2020 
Olympics, based on factors like athlete achievements, performance trend, progression, 
high performance age and comparative analysis with other players/potential international 
competitors is done. Furthermore, a review mechanism is in place, wherein, in addition 
to the above mentioned criteria, targets and intermediate milestones are fixed for the 
individuals for their continuation under the scheme. Sportspersons who fail to achieve 
the targets despite providing additional support and adequate time are dropped from 
the scheme. Based on the analysis, the TOPS athlete requirement is assessed and 
provided with holistic support in consultation with the National Sports Federation 
concerned and ex-eminent sportspersons from the concerned sports. At present, 71 
athletes have been identified for assistance under TOPS.
However, selection of athletes for participation in international sports events 
including Olympics is a continuous process. National Sports Federations (NSFs) 
are primarily responsible for judicious selection of national teams for participation 
in major international events including the Olympics, based on merit and with the 
objective of enhancing national prestige and bringing glory to the country. Further, 
participation of athletes included in TOPS in Tokyo Olympics 2020 is dependent on 
the qualification criteria prescribed by the concerned international sports federations 
for their respective sports disciplines, which are to be achieved by these athletes 
before they are selected. Since Olympic qualifiers are still going on, therefore, list 
of athletes to participate in Tokyo Olympics 2020 has not been finalized.

150. SHRI PARTAP SINGH BAJWA: Will the Minister of DeFeNCe be pleased 
to state:
(a) whether the Rafale Jets contract was concluded under the Inter-Governmental 
Agreement (IGA) route;
(b) if so, does the Rafale contract include a sovereign guarantee provided by

THe MINISTeR OF DeFeNCe (SHRIMATI NIRMAlA SITHARAMAN): (a) 
to (c) An Inter-Governmental Agreement (IGA) was signed on 23rd September, 
2016 between the Government of India and the Government of French Republic 
for the procurement of 36 Rafale fighter aircraft in fly-away condition, along with 
an initial consignment of weapons, maintenance support through Performance Based 
logistic (PBl), Simulator and associated equipment. In the 36 Rafale IGA, the 
French Government has provided a ‘letter of Comfort’ signed by the French Prime 
Minister. The provision in the IGA along with letter of Comfort provide adequate 
safeguards to the Government of India.

2016 between the Government of India and the Government of French Republic 
for the procurement of 36 Rafale fighter aircraft in fly-away condition, along with 
an initial consignment of weapons, maintenance support through Performance Based 
logistic (PBl), Simulator and associated equipment.

protection of the classified information and the material exchanged under IGA shall 
be governed by the provisions of the Security Agreement signed between Government 
of India and Government of France on 25th January, 2008. The Supply protocol for 
36 Rafale has provision for Commercial Confidentiality.

152. SHRI G.C. CHANDRASHeKHAR: Will the Minister of DRINKING WATeR 
AND SANITATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has been implementing Swachh Bharat Mission to 
provide access to toilet facilities;

356 Written Answers to [RAJyA SABHA] Unstarred Questions
(b) if so, the details thereof including physical and financial progress during the 
last three years, State-wise;
(c) whether some States have provided fake data, to show their States as Open 
Defecation Free;
(d) if so, current status of ODF districts, State-wise; and
(e) the other steps taken by the Government to improve sanitation in the country?
THe MINISTeR OF STATe IN THe MINISTR y  OF DRINKING WATeR 
AND SANITATION (SHRI RAMeSH CHANDAPPA JIGAJINAGI): (a) and (b) 
The Government had launched the Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) [(SBM(G)] 
with effect from 2nd October, 2014 with the aim to achieve universal sanitation 
coverage by 2nd October, 2019 by ensuring that all rural households in the country 
have access to toilet facilities. The focus of the scheme is on behavior change and 
usage of toilets. State/uT-wise number of individual households latrines (IHHls) 
constructed as per the data reported by the States/uTs on the Integrated Management 
Information System (IMIS) of SBM(G) and the funds released by the Government 
of India to the States/uTs during the last three years under SBM(G) are given in 
the Statement-I (See below). 
(c) and (d)  As per the SBM(G) guidelines, villages and districts declare 
themselves Open Defecation Free (ODF) through a rigorous process of self-declaration, 
followed by a multi-level decentralized verification process by the districts and States. 
Further, as per National Annual Rural Sanitation Survey (NARSS) 2017-18, conducted 
by an independent agency, 95.6% of ODF verified villages were confirmed to be 
ODF. State/uT-wise number of districts which have been declared Open Defecation 
Free (ODF) as on 31.01.2010 are given in the Statement-II.
(e) Since the launch of the Swachh Bharat Mission in 2014, States have made 
tremendous progress with reference to rural sanitation. While sanitation is State 
subject, Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation supports State Governments in 
the implementation of the SBM. Some focus areas are as follows:–
 ● Focus is being given on community based collective behavior change 
by massive campaigning at the national and State level. 
 ● Focus is also on the outcome of ODF villages, and not only on 
construction of individual toilets. 
 ● Given the vast socio-economic-cultural diversity of India, and also from 
the point of view of promoting innovations, the programme provides

flexibility to the States to choose the strategy best suited to them in 
its implementation. 
 ● Greater emphasis is being given on capacity building, especially in 
community approaches and programme management, by imparting 
training to the States and selected organisations called Key Resource 
Centres (KRCs), involving District Collectors to provide leadership to 
the programme at the district level. 
 ● The programme is being run as a jan andolan with cooperation of all 
sections of the society including the NGOs, corporates, youth etc. The 
Panchayats are being actively involved.
 ● Sanitation is being prioritized amongst the overall development agenda. 
The Government has taken a decision to prioritise all Centrally Sponsored 
Schemes in ODF villages. Various other development schemes are being 
converged with the sanitation outcomes.

Wildlife crime data bank
153. SHRIMATI V ANDANA CHA V AN: Will the Minister of eNVIRONMeNT, 
FOReST AND ClIMATe CHANGe be pleased to state:
(a) whether there has been an increase in the number of wildlife crimes in the 
last three years, and if so, the details thereof;
(b) the functions of the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau as per the ‘Wildlife 
(Protection) Act, 1972’;
(c) whether the wildlife crime data bank has been established as per Section 
38Z(1)(i) of the ‘Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972’;
(d) if so, the manner in which wildlife crime data bank aided the Wildlife Crime 
Control Bureau combat wildlife crime; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor and the expected data by when the wildlife crime 
data bank will be established?
THe MINISTe R OF STATe  IN THe  MINISTRy  OF eNVIRONMe NT, FORe ST 
AND ClIMATe CHANGe (DR. MAHeSH SHARMA): (a) As per available records 
in the Ministry, there is no increase in the number of wildlife crimes in the last 
three years.
(b) The functions of the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau as per the Wildlife 
(Protection) Act, 1972 are as follows:–
(i) Collect and collate intelligent related to organised wildlife crime activities 
and to disseminate the same to that State and other enforcement agencies 
for immediate action so as to apprehend the criminals and to establish 
a centralized wildlife crime data bank.
(ii) Co-ordination of actions by various officers, State Governments and other 
authorities in connection with the enforcement of the provisions of this 
Act, either directly or through regional and border units set up by the 
Bureau.

Re. Notices on [4 February, 2019]   different issues 361
(iii) Implementation of obligations under the various International Conventions 
and Protocols that are in force at present or which may be ratified or 
acceded to by India in future.
(iv) Assistance to concerned authorities in foreign countries and concerned 
International organisations to facilities co-ordination and universal action 
for wildlife crime control.
(v) Develop infrastructure and capacity building for scientific and professional 
investigation into wildlife crimes and assist State Governments to ensure 
success in prosecutions related to wildlife crimes.
(vi) Advice the Government of India on issues relating to wildlife crimes 
having National and International ramifications, and suggest changes 
required in relevant policy and laws from time to time.
(c) Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) has developed online Wildlife Crime 
Database Management System which is an interactive database driven web based 
module to invite data pertaining to wildlife crime from the divisional offices of the 
States directly to the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB).
(d) and (e) The ID and password have been provided to State Forest and Police 
officials for updating and viewing the data. State officials and Wildlife Crime Control 
Bureau (WCCB) can analyze crimes related to wildlife by charting out trade route, 
modus operandi of criminals, same criminals involved in different crime and area 
of operation as well as specific species targeted by particular criminals etc. It is to 
mention that wildlife crime is an organised crime with backward and forward linkages. 
The wildlife crime database of Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) is very helpful 
to combat wildlife crime by identifying the criminals operating in geographical areas 
based on which advisories and alerts are issued to State enforcement authorities for 
enforcement and preventive action.

भारत में , लूओं की वस्थवतयााँ सामान्यतः माचत से जुलाई की अववध क े िौरान उत्पन्न होती हैं। यह पाया 
गया है कक ग्रीष्मकाल (अप्रैल-मई-जून) क े  िौरान पंजाब, वहमाचल प्रिेश, उत्तराखंड, किल्ली, हररयाणा , 
राजस्थान, उत्तर प्रिेश, गुजरात , मध्य प्रिेश, छत्तीसगढ़, वबहार , झारखंड , पविम बंगाल, ओवडशा और 
तेलंगाना राज्यों में वस्थत स्टेशनों तथा  मराठवाडा , वविभत, मध्य महाराष्ट्र मौसम-वैज्ञावनक उपखंडों और

िौरान क े वल पलक् कड, कोझीकोड और कन्नूर वजलों में अप्रैल-मई 2016 क े  िौरान पांच किनों क े  वलए लू 
की वस्थवत घोवर्षत की गई थी। 
(ख) वपछले सौ से अवधक वर्षों क े  िौरान भारत क े  अवधकांश भागों में प्रेवक्षत तापमान ग्लोबल वार्ममग क े  
अनुरूप तापमान में वृवि क े  रुझान का संक ेत िेते हैं। जलवायु मॉडल संक े त िे रहे हैं कक ग्रीनहाउस गैसों

तेज लूओं  (एचडबल्यू) की कोई सावतभौवमक पररभार्षा नहीं है। वभन्न-वभन्न िेशों में तेज लूओं की वभन्न-

अवधक गमत मौसम क े  अंतराल का प्रवतवनवधत्व कर ती  हैं। अपेक्षाक ृ त उच्च तीव्रता की गमत हवाओं  को तेज  
लूओं (एसएचडबल्यू) क े  रूप में वगीक ृ त ककया जाता है। भारत में गमत हवाओं  को पररभावर्षत करने क े  
वलए प्रयुक् त नवीनतम मानिंड वर्षत 1971-2000 की अववध क े  जलवायु -वैज्ञावनक मूल्यों पर आधाररत 
हैं और ये नीचे किए गए हैं: 
 
अवधकतम तापमान (टीमैक्स ) क े  आधार पर गमत हवाएं  घोवर्षत करने क े  मानिंड: 
 
ककसी भी स्टेशन पर गमत हवाएं तभी घोवर्षत की  जाती हैं जब मैिानी क्षेत्रों क े स्टेशनों में वास्तववक 
टीमैक्स 40° सें. और पहाडी क्षेत्रों क े  स्टेशनों में वास्तववक टीमैक्स 30° सें. हो। हालांकक , जब तटीय 
स्टेशनों में टीमैक्स 40° सें. और अन्य स्टेशनों में 45° सें. होता है , तो इन वस्थवतयों को गमत हवाएं

ii. वास्तववक टीमैक्स सामान्य टीमैक्स से 7°सें. तक  अवधक होता है तो: तेज लूएं  
 
जब सामान्य टीमैक्स 40° सें.  से अवधक  होता है और

वायु ᮧदूषण पर वनािᲨ का ᮧभाव  
35. ᮰ीमती वंदना च᭪हाणः  
 
 ᭍या पयाᭅवरण, वन और जलवायु पᳯरवतᭅन मंᮢी यह बताने कᳱ क ृ पा करᱶगे ᳰकः 
 
 
(क) ᭍या िपछले तीन वषᲄ मᱶ वनािᲨ कᳱ सं᭎या मᱶ वृि᳍ ᱟई है और यᳰद हां, तो त᭜संबंधी ᭣यौरा ᭍या है;  
 
(ख) वनािᲨ कᳱ सं᭎या मᱶ वृि᳍ को रोकने क े िलए उठाए गए कदमᲂ का ᭣यौरा ᭍या है;  
 
(ग) वनािᲨ क े कारण वायु ᮧदूषण मᱶ ᳰकतने ᮧितशत वृि᳍ होती है;  
 
(घ) िपछले दो वषᲄ हेतु वनािᲨ िनयंᮢण और ᮧबंधन योजना क े अंतगᭅत ᳰकतनी रािश आबंᳯटत तथा जारी कᳱ 
 गई; और  
(ङ) ᭍या मंᮢालय कᳱ रा᳦ीय हᳯरत अिधकरण ᳇ारा ᳰदये गए िनदᱷश क े अनुसार वनािᲨ कᳱ रोकथाम और 
 िनयंᮢण पर ᭟यान देने क े िलए एक रा᳦ीय वनािᲨ ᮧबंधन योजना लाने कᳱ योजना है? 
 
उत्  तर 
 
पयाᭅवरण, वन और जलवायु पᳯरवतᭅन राज्  य मंᮢी  
(डॉ. महेश शमाᭅ) 
 
 
(क) जी, नहᱭ। वनािᲨ कᳱ घटनाᲐ  कᳱ संख्  या िविभन्  न कारकᲂ क े आधार पर वषᭅ-दर-वषᭅ बदलती रहती 
है। सूखी पिᱫयᲂ, टहिनयᲂ, पाइन नीड᭨स आᳰद जैसी ज्  वलनशील सामिᮕयᲂ क े एकिᮢत होने सिहत 
िविभन्  न ᮧाक ृ ितक और मानवजिनत कारणᲂ से हर साल गᳶमयᲂ मᱶ वनािᲨ कᳱ घटनाएं होती हᱹ। जब 
भी वनािᲨ का पता लगता है भारतीय वन सवᱷᭃण (एफएसआई), देहरादून, राज्  य क े वन िवभागᲂ 
तथा अन्  य पंजीक ृ त उपयोगकताᭅᲐ को उपᮕह आधाᳯरत वनािᲨ चेतावनी को ᮧसाᳯरत करता है। िपछले 
तीन वषᲄ क े दौरान सभी राज्  य/संघ राज्  य ᭃेᮢᲂ क े वन िवभागᲂ को जारी कᳱ गई वनािᲨ  
चेताविनयᲂ का िववरण अनुबंध-I मᱶ ᳰदया गया है। 
(ख) वनᲂ कᳱ सुरᭃा और ᮧबंधन तथा वनािᲨ क े िनवारण/िनयंᮢण का दाियत्  व मुख्  य ᱨ प से संबंिधत 
राज् य/संघ राज्  य ᭃेᮢ कᳱ सरकार का है।  
मंᮢालय ने वनािᲨ  क े संबंध मᱶ राष्  ᮝीय कायᭅ-योजना तैयार कᳱ है और उसे वनािᲨ  क े ᮧभावी 
िनवारण और ᮧबंधन क े िलए उिचत कारᭅवाई हेतु सभी राज्  यᲂ/संघ राज्  य ᭃेᮢᲂ को भेजा है।  
(ग) वनािᲨ काबᭅन-डाइऑक ्   साइड और प᳷टक ु लेट मैटर छोड़ती है िजसक े कारण वायु ᮧदूषण होता है। 
तथािप, इस मंᮢालय ᳇ारा वनािᲨ क े कारण वायु ᮧदूषण क े ᮧितशत को िनधाᭅᳯरत करने क े िलए कोई 
अध्  ययन नहᱭ ᳰकया गया है।

(क) : राष्  ᮝीय वायु गुणवत्  ता िनगरानी कायᭅᮓम (एनएएमपी) क े तहत देश भर क े 29 राज्  यᲂ और 6

ᱟआ ᱨ झान, 5 शहरᲂ मᱶ घटता ᱟआ सांᮤण और 29 शहरᲂ मᱶ घटता-बढ़ता ᱟआ ᱨ झान ᳰदखाई पड़ा है।

(क) और (ख)  भारत जलवायु पᳯरवतᭅन संबंधी अंतर-शासकᳱय पैनल (आईपीसीसी) का एक पᭃ कार 
है, जो जलवायु पᳯरवतᭅन से संबंिधत िव᭄ान के आकलन के िलए एक अंतर-शासकᳱय िनकाय है। 
आईपीसीसी कᳱ स्  थापना वषᭅ 1988 मᱶ संयुक्  त राष्  ᮝ पयाᭅवरण कायᭅᮓम और िवश्  व मौसम िव᭄ान संगठन 
᳇ारा संयुक्  त ᱧप से कᳱ गई थी, िजसका उ᳎ेश्  य नीित-िनमाᭅताᲐ  को जलवायु पᳯरवतᭅन से संबंिधत 
वै᭄ािनक आकलनᲂ, उसकᳱ अपेᭃाᲐ  और संभािवत भावी जोिखमᲂ के िवषय मᱶ िनयिमत ᱨ प से जानकारी 
उपलब्  ध कराना और अनुकूलन तथा उपशमन कायᭅनीितयᲂ को कायाᭅि᭠वत करना है। भारत सिहत दुिनया 
भर क े वै᭄ािनक आईपीसीसी कᳱ आकलन ᳯरपोटᲄ मᱶ योगदान करते हᱹ।  
 आईपीसीसी ᳇ारा अक ्   तूबर, 2018 मᱶ इंिचअन, कोᳯरया गणतंᮢ मᱶ 1.50c के वैि᳡ क तापन से 
संबंिधत एक िवशेष ᳯरपोटᭅ अनुमोᳰदत कᳱ गई थी। उस ᳯरपोटᭅ क े अनुसार, पूरी दुिनया मᱶ 1.50c क े 
औसत तापन से कई अन्  य संभािवत दुष्  ᮧभावᲂ मᱶ लू या गमᱮ कᳱ लहरᲂ और भारी वषाᭅ कᳱ घटनाᲐ  का 
जोिखम उत्  पन्  न होता है; और तापन को 20c कᳱ अपेᭃ ा 1.50c तक सीिमत रखने से इन जोिखमᲂ को 
कम करने मᱶ मदद िमल सकती है। इस ᳯरपोटᭅ के अनुसार, वैि᳡ क तापन को 1.50c तक सीिमत रखने 
हेतु भूिम, ऊजाᭅ, उ᳒ ोग, भवनᲂ, पᳯरवहन और शहरᲂ मᱶ ᮤुत गित से और दूरगामी पᳯरणाम वाले 
पᳯरवतᭅनᲂ कᳱ अपेᭃ ा होगी। आदशᭅ उपायᲂ के ᱨ प मᱶ, वषᭅ 2030 तक मनुष्  यᲂ ᳇ारा उत्  पन्  न वैि᳡ क

54. ᮰ी िहशे लाचुंगपा : 
᭍या पयाᭅवरण, वन और जलवायु पᳯरवतᭅन मंᮢी यह बताने कᳱ क ृ पा करᱶगे ᳰक : 
 
(क) गत तीन वषᲄ मᱶ देश मᱶ बाघ अभयारण्  यᲂ मᱶ से ᮧत्  येक अभयारण्  य मᱶ ᳰकतने बाघᲂ कᳱ मृत्  यु ᱟई है;  
(ख) ᳰकतने बाघ मारे गए और ᳰकतने बाघᲂ कᳱ रोग क े कारण मृत्  यु ᱟई;  
(ग)  बाघᲂ को िशकाᳯरयᲂ और रोग से बचाने क े िलए ᳰकए जा रहे ᮧयासᲂ का ब्  यौरा क ्   या है; और  
(घ) इस संबंध मᱶ राज्  य सरकार को ᳰकस स्  तर कᳱ कᱶ ᮤीय सहायता ᮧाप्  त हो रही है? 
उत्  तर 
पयाᭅवरण, वन और जलवायु पᳯरवतᭅन राज्  य मंᮢी  
(डॉ. महेश शमाᭅ) 
(क) वषᭅ 2016, 2017 और 2018 क े दौरान बाघ ᳯरजवᲄ मᱶ 185 बाघᲂ कᳱ मृत्  यु ᱟई है। िववरण अनुबंध-। 
मᱶ ᳰदया गया है।  
(ख)  उक ्   त अविध क े दौरान संपुष्  ट कारणᲂ मᱶ से 119 बाघᲂ कᳱ मृत्  यु ᮧाक ृ ितक कारणᲂ, 51 कᳱ मृत्  यु अवैध 
िशकार क े कारण ᱟई, 40 कᳱ बाघ क े शरीर क े अंगᲂ कᳱ जब्  ती से पुि᳥ ᱟई जबᳰक 15 बाघᲂ कᳱ मृत्  यु 
अस्  वाभािवक कारणᲂ से ᱟई िजसे अवैध िशकार क े कारण नहᱭ कहा जा सकता है।  उक ्   त अविध क े दौरान 
बीमारी क े कारण बाघᲂ कᳱ मृत्  यु क े ᳰकसी मामले कᳱ पुि᳥ नहᱭ ᱟई है।  
(ग)  बाघᲂ कᳱ सुरᭃ ा क े िलए िनम्  निलिखत कदम उठाए गए हᱹ:- 
(i) सुरᭃ ा योजना तैयार करने संबंधी िजनेᳯरक ᳰदशािनदᱷश जो बाघ संरᭃ ण योजना का भाग है और 
वन्  यजीव (संरᭃ ण) अिधिनयम, 1972 क े अंतगᭅत अिनवायᭅ है। 
(ii) बाघ ᳯरजवᲄ कᳱ सुरᭃ ा आिडट करने क े िलए एक ᮧोटोकॉल ᮧारंभ ᳰकया गया है।  
(iii) सभी बाघ ᳯरजवᲄ को मानसून मᱶ गश्  त करने क े िलए परामᳶशका जारी कᳱ गई है।  
(iv) िबजली क े करंट लगने क े कारण मृत्  युदर से िनपटने क े िलए परामᳶशका पᳯरचािलत कᳱ गई है।  
(v) ᮧभावी ᭃ ेᮢ ᮧभुत् व और साथ ही जबावदेही सुिनि᳟ त करने क े िलए सभी बाघ ᳯरजवᲄ को M-STrIPES 
गश्  त अनुᮧयोग एंᮟाइड आधाᳯरत (बाघᲂ कᳱ गहन सुरᭃ ा और पाᳯरि᭭थ ितकᳱ ि᭭थित क े िलए िनगरानी 
ᮧणाली) उपलब्  ध कराई गई है।  
(vi) िवशेष पᳯरयोजना मᱶ मानव रिहत हवाई वाहन (यूएवी) का ᮧयोग ᳰकया गया है और ᭃ मता िनमाᭅण क े 
पश्  चात उपकरणᲂ का पहला सेट पन्  ना बाघ ᳯरजवᭅ को सᲅपा गया है।  
(vii) अवैध िशकार रोधी उपकरणᲂ कᳱ खरीद करने और कानूनी सहायता तथा आसूचना एकᮢ करने जैसी 
सहायता क े अलावा, िशकार-रोधी स्  टाफ कᳱ तैनाती, अवसंरचना िवकास क े िलए बाघ पᳯरयोजना कᳱ 
जारी कᱶ ᮤीय ᮧायोिजत स्  कᳱम क े तहत िवत्  तीय सहायता।  
(viii) हिथयार बनाने तथा िवशेष बाघ सुरᭃ ा बल तैनात करने क े िलए िवत्  तीय सहायता।  
(ix) बाघ ᳯरजवᲄ क े बाहर क े बाघ बᱟल संवेदनशील ᭃ ेᮢᲂ मᱶ गश्  त करने क े िलए राष्  ᮝीय बाघ संरᭃ ण 
ᮧािधकरण (एनटीसीए) क े जᳯरए अनुदान ᮧदान करना।

सोमवार, 4 फरवरी, 2019  को उत्तर के ललए 
 
 
संसद सदस्यों के ललए सरकार द्वारा ननयुक्त ककए गए ववधायी सहायक  
 
 
85.  श्री संजय सेठ:  
 
 क्या संसदीय कायय मंत्री यह बताने की कृपा करेंगे कक:  
 
(क ) क्या सरकार को इस बात की जानकारी है कक बह ुत से देश अपने संसद सदस्यों को उनके संसदीय कायय के लिए 
योग्य विधायी और नीतत अनुसंधान सहायक प्रदान करते हैं ; 
 
(ख) हमारी सरकार द्िारा ऐसी योजनाओं का अनुसरण नहीं ककए  जाने के क्या कारण हैं ; 
 
(ग) यदद ऐसी कोई योजना है, तो तत्संबंधी ब्यौरा क्या है; और 
 
(घ) क्या संसद  सदस्यों के  कायायिय में पयायप्त संख्या में अनुसंधान  सहायकों  की  तनयुक्क्त करने  की  योजनाएं हैं ताकक  
िह अपने कर्त्यव्यों का  तनियहन बेहतर  जानकारी  के  साथ कर  सक ें? 
 
 
उत्तर 
 
 
संसदीय कायय मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री; और 
सांख्ख्यकी तथा काययक्रम कायायन्वयन मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री  
(श्री ववजय गोयल)  
 
 
(क ) से (घ)   अपने जन प्रतततनधधयों को  उनकी  अपेक्षाओं और क्स्थततयों के  अनुसार िेतन  और सुविधाओं  का  तनधायरण करने  
के  लिए प्रत्येक देश  के  अपने अधधतनयम  और तनयम होते  हैं।  संसद  सदस्य िेतन , भर्त्ा और पेंशन अधधतनयम , 1954 और 
उसके  अंतगयत बनाए गए तनयम, क्जन्हें संिैधातनक  उपबंधों  के  अनुसरण  में अधधतनयलमत  ककया  गया है, संसद  सदस्यों के  
िेतन  और भर्त्ों का  तनधायरण करते  हैं।  समय-समय पर गदित  की  जाने िािी दोनों सदनों  की  संयुक्त सलमतत  धिककत्सा 
सुविधाओं , यात्रा और दैतनक  भर्त्े, आिास और टेिीफोन सुविधाओं , तनिायिन क्षेत्र संबंधी  भर्त्े, कायायिय व्यय भर्त्े इत्यादद

 व᭠यजीव अपराध डेटा बᱹक 
153. ᮰ीमती वंदना च᭪हाण:
᭍या पयाᭅवरण, वन और जलवायु पᳯरवतᭅन मंᮢी यह बताने कᳱ कृ पा करᱶगे ᳰक:
(क) ᭍या िपछले तीन वषᲄ के दौरान व᭠यजीव अपराधᲂ कᳱ सं᭎या मᱶ वृि᳃ ᱟई है, और यᳰद हां, तो 
त᭜संबंधी ᭣यौरा ᭍या है;  
(ख) व᭠य जीव (संरᭃण) अिधिनयम, 1972 के अनुसार व᭠यजीव अपराध िनयंᮢण ᭣यूरो के कायᭅ ᭍या 
है; 
(ग) ᭍या व᭠यजीव (संरᭃण) अिधिनयम, 1972 कᳱ धारा 38य(1)(झ) के अनुसार व᭠यजीव अपराध 
डेटा बᱹक कᳱ ᭭थापना कᳱ गई है; 
(घ) यᳰद हां, तो व᭠यजीव अपराध को कम करने क े िलए व᭠यजीव अपराध डेटा बᱹक ने ᳰकस ᮧकार 
व᭠यजीव अपराध िनयंᮢण ᭣यूरो कᳱ सहायता कᳱ; और  
(ङ) यᳰद नहᱭ, तो इसक े ᭍या कारण हᱹ और व᭠यजीव अपराध डेटा बᱹक कᳱ ᭭थापना ᳰकस ितिथ तक 
ᳰकये जाने कᳱ अपेᭃा ह ै ? 
उत्  तर 
पयाᭅवरण, वन और जलवायु पᳯरवतᭅन राज्  य मंᮢी 
(डᱼ म हेश शमाᭅ) 
(क) मंᮢालय मᱶ उपलब्  ध ᳯरकोडᭅ के अनुसार, िपछले तीन वषᲄ से वन्  यजीव अपराधᲂ कᳱ संख्  या मᱶ कोई 
वृि᳍ नहᱭ ᱟई है। 
(ख)  वन्  यजीव (संरᭃण) अिधिनयम, 1972 के अनुसार वन्  यजीव अपराध िनयंᮢण ब्  यूरो के कायᭅ इस 
ᮧकार हᱹ: 
i. संगᳯठत वन्  यजीव अपराध गितिविधयᲂ से संबंिधत आसूचना को एकिᮢत और समेᳰकत करना और
तुरंत कारᭅवाई के िलए उसे राज्  य और अन्  य ᮧवतᭅन एजᱶिसयᲂ को ᮧसाᳯरत करना ताᳰक अपरािधयᲂ
को पकड़ा जा सक े और एक के न्  ᮤीकृ त वन्  यजीव अपराध डेटा बᱹक स्  थािपत ᳰकया जा सक े।
ii. इस अिधिनयम के ᮧावधानᲂ क े ᮧवतᭅन के संबंध मᱶ िविभन्  न अिधकाᳯरयᲂ, राज्  य सरकारᲂ और
अन्  य ᮧािधकाᳯरयᲂ ᳇ारा कᳱ गई कारᭅवाईयᲂ को या तो सीधे तौर पर या ब्  यूरो ᳇ारा स्  थािपत
ᭃेᮢीय और सीमा इकाइयᲂ के माध्  यम से समि᭠वत करना।
iii. िविभन्  न अंतरराष्  ᮝीय सम्  मेलनᲂ और ᮧोटोकॉल जो वतᭅम ान  समय मᱶ लागू हᱹ या जो भिवष्  य मᱶ
भारत ᳇ारा मंजूर और स्  वीकृ त हो सकते हᱹ के तहत दाियत्  वᲂ का कायाᭅन्  वयन।
iv. वन्  यजीव अपराध िनयंᮢण के िलए समन्  वय और सावᭅभौिमक कारᭅवाई को आसान बनाने के िलए
िवदेशᲂ और संबंिधत अंतरराष्  ᮝीय संगठनᲂ मᱶ संबंिधत अिधकाᳯरयᲂ कᳱ सहायता।

v. वन्  यजीव अपराधᲂ कᳱ वै᭄ािनक और व्  यवसाियक जांच के िलए आधाᳯरक संरचना और ᭃमता
िनमाᭅण का िवकास करना और वन्  यजीव अपराधᲂ से संबंिधत अिभयोगᲂ मᱶ सफलता सुिनि᳟त करने
के िलए राज्  य सरकार कᳱ सहायता करना।
vi. भारत सरकार को वन्  यजीव अपराधᲂ से जुड़े राष्  ᮝीय और अंतरराष्  ᮝीय ᮧभाव वाले मामलᲂ पर
सलाह देना और समय-समय पर संगत नीित और कानून मᱶ अपेिᭃत पᳯरवतᭅनᲂ को ᮧस्  तािवत
करना।
(ग)  वन्  यजीव अपराध िनयंᮢण ब्  यूरो (डब्  ल्  यूसीसीबी) ने ऑनलाइन वन्  यजीव अपराध डेटाबेस ᮧबंधन 
ᮧणाली िवकिसत कᳱ है जो वन्  यजीव अपराध िनयंᮢण ब्  यूरो (डब्  ल्  यूसीसीबी) को सीधे भेजने के िलए 
राज्  यᲂ के ᮧभागीय कायाᭅलयᲂ से वन्  यजीव अपराध से संबंिधत आंकड़ᲂ को मंगवाने क े िलए पारि᭭परक 
डेटाबेस संचािलत वेब आधाᳯरत मॉडयूल है।  
(घ) और (ड.)  राज्  य वन और पुिलस अिधकाᳯरयᲂ को अ᳒तनीकरण और डेटा देखने क े िलए आईडी 
और पासवडᭅ ᮧदान ᳰकए गए हᱹ। वन्  यजीव से जुड़े अपराध व्  यापार मागᭅ, अपरािधयᲂ कᳱ कायᭅ-ᮧणाली दूसरे 
अपराधᲂ मᱶ भ ी  उन्  हᱭ अपरािधयᲂ के शािमल होने और संचालन का ᭃेᮢ और इसके साथ-साथ खास 
अपरािधयᲂ ᳇ारा लिᭃत िविशष्  ट जाितयᲂ कᳱ जानकारी तैयार करक े वन्  यजीवᲂ से संबंिधत अपराधᲂ का 
राज्  य पदािधकारी और वन्  यजीव अपराध िनयंᮢण ब्  यूरो (डब्  ल्  यूसीसीबी) िवश्  लेषण कर सकते हᱹ। यहां ये 
उल्  लेख ᳰकया जाता है ᳰक वन्  यजीव अपराध एक संगᳯठत अपराध है िजसके साथ उसक े िपछले और 
भिवष्  य मᱶ संपकᭅ जुड़े ᱟए है। वन्  यजीव अपराध िनयंᮢण ब्  यूरो (डब्  ल्  यूसीसीबी) के वन्  यजीव अपराध से 
संबंिधत डेटाबेस भौगोिलक ᭃेᮢᲂ मᱶ सᳰᮓय अपरािधयᲂ कᳱ पहचान करक े वन्  यजीव अपराध से िनपटने मᱶ 
बᱟत मददगार है िजसके आधार पर राज्  य ᮧवतᭅन अिधकाᳯरयᲂ को ᮧवतᭅन और िनवारक कारᭅवाई के िलए
